content_html_sanitized:
As it says on every page of MarijuanaNews, the best two word explanation for Marijuana Prohibition is bad journalism, but I don’t think that “journalism” is relevant to the New York Post.

 

Whatever it is that they are doing seems to be about ideological gotchas. The most obvious example of that is the latest product of their regular star columnist, Amanda Devine: “Trump knows the dangers of addiction — he must reject Big Weed’s push to reclassify marijuana.”

 

What a mess!

 

She begins with “President Trump is reportedly considering reclassifying marijuana federally as a less dangerous drug. You know it’s a bad idea if Joe Biden was for it. That’s the case with the mad push for marijuana reform, which Biden promised in a cynical grab for young voters in his State of the Union address last year.”

 

Perhaps she has forgotten, or hopes that her readers have forgotten, but Donald Trump voted for complete legalization last year in Florida.

 

And Trump Criticizes Low-Level Marijuana Arrests, Predicts Passage of Amendment 3 Legalization Initiative

 

It needed 60% of the popular vote, but it fell short with a little less than 55.9% . I am sure that Trump had only the most idealistic motives, but he got 56.%, slightly more than the evil weed.

 

Devine: “But now President Trump is reported to be open to fulfilling Biden’s promise to reclassify marijuana as a less dangerous Schedule III drug, which would benefit the $33 billion industry by giving them tax deductions and expanding their market.”

 

If your sole motivation is to raise taxes on marijuana businesses this is a messy way to do it. At no point here does she seem to understand the scheduling process or what is being proposed. Schedule one drugs supposedly have no recognized medical use.

 

Of course, the marijuana reform movement and medical marijuana patients have not been blocking the research and have never had the ability to do so.

 

Moving it to Schedule 2 would keep the tax penalties and put it in the same risk category with Fentanyl, which is absurd.

See

Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

 

Devine: “According to The Wall Street Journal, Trump told donors he was considering the “de-scheduling” of marijuana at a $1 million-a-plate fundraiser at his Bedminster golf club in New Jersey this month that was attended by Kim Rivers, the chief executive of one of the largest marijuana companies, Trulieve. Trulieve and its ilk pretend that marijuana reforms are for altruistic medical reasons rather than about growing their profits.”

 

And everyone knows how much President Trump is against companies making a profit as a result of giving campaign contributions. Just ask Elon!

 

Devine: “Medical marijuana was the bait-and-switch trap when states started legalizing pot more than a decade ago.”

 

Actually, it was in 1996 with California’s Proposition 215, but what’s a few decades when you’re not in pain, or vomiting, or dying of AIDS because you have lost your appetite??

See Massive New Study of California Cannabis Users Shows Continuum Between Recreational and Medical Use

 

Devine: Now recreational use has exploded to the point where it has overtaken alcohol, and there’s still no sound science on the benefits of medical marijuana.

From 199917 AIDS Organizations Write Drug Czar Urging Medical Marijuana Not Be Delayed By IOM Report; "Terminally ill patients cannot afford to wait for years of research to prove something they already know: Medical marijuana works."

Plus Medicinal cannabis policies and practices around the world

 

‘Complicated subject’

Devine: “The president confirmed last week to reporters at the White House that his administration is “looking at reclassification” and intends to make a decision soon. “It’s a very complicated subject base,” he said. “I’ve heard great things having to do with medical and bad things having to do with just about everything else.”

See

Trump moving closer to decision on making weed less criminal in eyes of federal government: sources

Devine: “Trump is a teetotaler…He credits his late older brother Fred Trump Jr., with his decision not to drink or take drugs. Fred struggled with alcoholism, and died in 1981, aged 42, as a consequence of his disease. Trump learned from his brother’s mistakes: “I never had a drink of alcohol. I don’t smoke, and I’m a hard worker. Well, he worked, but he just had the curse, you know, and it was tough.”

 

Devine: Marijuana is a disaster. It’s infinitely worse than alcohol on every metric, especially mental health.

From the Centers for Disease Control: “Excessive alcohol use is a leading preventable cause of death in the United States. About 178,000 people die from excessive drinking each year.”

They do not report any marijuana immediately related deaths.

 

Devine: “The scientific evidence is incontrovertible that marijuana triggers psychosis in susceptible people.

See The Great Debate: Marijuana vs Alcohol

And

Alcohol-related psychosis (ARP) is a well-established complication of heavy alcohol use,

 

Devine: For example, a large-scale Danish study published in the American Journal of Psychiatry in 2017 found that up to 30% of young men’s schizophrenia could have been prevented if they had not used pot.

See Scientific American Magazine Publishes Article by Respected Journalist on Study Showing Brain Changes Came Before Not After “Drug” Use. Difficult to Ignore.

 

Devine: An episode triggered by marijuana use was associated with a 47% chance of a person schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, with the highest risk for Another longitudinal study of 50,000 Swedes that began in 1987 found that marijuana users were twice as likely as non-users to develop psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia. Heavy users had a six times greater risk.”

 

MarijuanaNews note: “Schizophrenia affects around 0.3–0.7% of the general population at some point in life (ie lifetime prevalence), [1] or 21 million people worldwide as of 2020”.

So if marijuana really did cause schizophrenia, and that is not proven, and if it was possible to completely eliminate marijuana, which prohibition spectacularly failed to do, it might have prevented or delayed schizophrenia in .02 of the population.

 

Devine: And it was a far less potent drug than it is now.

Marijuana of 40 years ago had about a 5% concentration of THC, the intoxicating component of cannabis, but today’s industrial products such as gummies, vapes and pre-rolled joints can be as high as 99% THC.

See The Perils of Potent Pot Party Line: Blaming Marijuana Legalization for Increase in THC Levels

 

Devine: The stench of pot wafting through blue cities like New York is a hallmark of chaos and disorder. It’s the opposite of President Trump’s law and order image.

 

Devine: Just say no to Big Dope — and its push for even more legal marijuana

So it is hard to believe he would bow to Big Weed and normalize this insidious drug further. Unlike his predecessor, Trump understands on a personal level the perils of addiction.

 

Devine: You’d think with the drug problems that have afflicted the lives of both his adult children, Hunter and Ashley, Biden might have had more sense, but pandering to Big Weed was a running theme of his presidency, with executive orders and performative pardons for federal marijuana possession (not one person was in jail for possession alone).

 

Marijuananews note: No one goes to Federal prison for Possession alone, because only people arrested on Federal property would be subject to Federal jurisdiction. All of the other prosecutions would be under state laws. There are still over 200,000 marijuana possession arrests every year.

 

Devine: Thankfully, wise heads inside the Drug Enforcement Administration dragged the chain long enough to stop Biden’s plan to reclassify marijuana. The drug lobby has redoubled efforts under Trump, but the signs don’t look good for them with the confirmation last month of the new DEA administrator, Terrance Cole.  Much to the disappointment of pot advocates, marijuana was nowhere to be seen on his list of “strategic priorities” announced after he took office, which included combating drug trafficking, Mexican cartels, fentanyl and drug-fueled violence. Even better, in a post on LinkedIn last year, he wrote:

“Everybody knows my stance on marijuana after 30 plus years in law enforcement, so don’t even ask!” He added anti-drug hashtags #justsayno, #disorders, #notlegal4distribution, #healthissues, #thinblueline and #backtheblue

Okay, but what does all this have to do with whether cannabis has medical use?

Nothing.
